comparison: Both support the technical robustness of the segmentation pipeline (C2, C20, C56, C59-C60, C87-C89, C94-C95). OpenEval evaluates the full pipeline including classification (C24-C27, C64-C68) as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers accept the segmentation but express concerns about classification accuracy in R2.

OpenEval finds classification performance (88% average, 95% median, C24-C27, C64-C67) SUPPORTED with appropriate validation. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, stating '88% accuracy seems relatively low' and expressing concern that '12% miss-classification could have quite some effect on the conclusions.'

OpenEval finds quantitative growth measurements (C16-C19, C21-C23) SUPPORTED with statistical robustness. Peer reviewers rate related claims UNCERTAIN, noting 'many precise measurements without inserting them in a proper context' and questioning the biological utility of genotype comparisons.

OpenEval finds cell-type-specific proliferation analysis and PCA (C28-C33, C50-C55) SUPPORTED with clear mechanistic insights. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, unable to reproduce Figure 3 PCA results and questioning what explains 94% variation in PC1, plus concerns about biological context.

OpenEval finds cell orientation analysis (C34-C36, C71-C72) SUPPORTED with statistical validation via Hartigans' dip test. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning 'what happens when a cell is round' and how randomized distributions in round cells were addressed.

Both support the visual inspection findings on cell division patterns and cambial activity (C37-C43, C73-C79). OpenEval notes reliance on qualitative assessment; peer reviewers accept validity but suggest additional quantitative analyses like separating cell expansion from proliferation contributions.

Perfect agreement. Both find phloem pole patterning analysis (C3, C44-C45, C63) SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates Bayesian analysis and GUS staining; peer reviewers accept these findings as valid examples from the cellular resolution atlas.

OpenEval rates speculative mechanisms (C46-C47, C70, C80-C82) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting lack of experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate similar speculative claims (C46-C47, C70, C80-C81) as SUPPORTED, treating them as reasonable hypotheses rather than requiring validation.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty. Both rate generalizability claims (C69) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes lack of validation on other tissue types; peer reviewers specifically request clarification on applicability to other organs/species like poplar cambium or maize roots.

OpenEval finds experimental framework and design (C8-C15, C58) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and justification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge the experimental setup.

OpenEval finds background information and literature context (C1, C4-C7, C83-C86, C91-C93) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge background claims.
OpenEval finds citations of prior molecular work (C48-C49) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge these literature references.

OpenEval includes computational scope (C61-C62) in pipeline validation as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers separately note these computational limitations as SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable constraints without challenging the analysis scope.
